cross_product_finding: Two distinct findings. (1) This page explicitly states 'Databases created on Couchbase Lite can share the same hierarchical structure as Capella databases. This makes it easier to sync data between mobile applications and applications built using Capella' - i.e. the DATA MODEL hierarchy (Database/Scope/Collection) is presented as directly cross-product-consistent with Capella (and by extension server/), unlike the access-control model, which per this stress test's premise is NOT shared. We could not mint a relation pointing at a specific Capella hierarchy concept id since none was given in our registry (only privilege/edition/role concepts were listed for Capella), but this is a strong signal that 'data model' vocabulary (scope/collection) is a better cross-product-reuse candidate than 'access control' vocabulary. (2) Database Encryption is Enterprise-Edition-gated (reusing the cbl:enterprise-edition concept minted in querybuilder.md for Predictive Query), but Database Full Sync - a comparable 'safety/reliability' feature - is NOT edition-gated, just off-by-default. This confirms CBL's Enterprise gate is applied selectively per-feature rather than as a blanket 'advanced reliability features' boundary.
notable_absence: No RBAC-privilege or role concept applies to opening/closing/encrypting a local database - the only 'access control' concern at this layer is the encryption key itself (an app-managed secret, not a granted permission), which the doc explicitly says Couchbase Lite does not persist ('It is the application's responsibility to manage the key and store it in a platform-specific secure store').
